question: A thermometer consistently reads 2°C higher than the actual temperature. This thermometer is _____________.
solution:
The correct answer is __precise but not accurate__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Precision__ refers to the consistency of measurements, meaning the thermometer gives the same reading repeatedly.
 
• The thermometer reads 2°C higher than the actual temperature each time.
 
• This indicates that while the thermometer is consistent (precise), it is not accurate because it does not show the true temperature.
 
• An accurate thermometer would display the true temperature.
 
• This distinction is important when selecting instruments for measurements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Accuracy vs Precision:**
 
 
• Accuracy relates to how close a measured value is to the actual value.
 
• Precision relates to how consistent measurements are when repeated under the same conditions.
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• A dartboard analogy: hitting the same spot repeatedly (even if it's not near the bullseye) indicates precision, while hitting the bullseye represents accuracy.
